questions.q: Write the reagents and conditions for the electrophilic chlorination of benzene. What is the role of the Lewis acid catalyst?
questions.a: Reagents: Benzene + Cl₂ with anhydrous FeCl₃ (or AlCl₃) in dark/room temperature. Role: FeCl₃ polarises Cl₂ to generate the electrophile Cl⁺ (via [FeCl₄]⁻ Cl⁺). A wrong answer like "FeCl₃ acts as a base" or "no catalyst needed" reveals confusion between electrophilic aromatic substitution and free radical halogenation of alkanes (node c12_chem_cbse_06_004).

questions.q: Chlorine is electron-withdrawing by inductive effect, yet it is ortho/para-directing in electrophilic substitution. Explain this apparent contradiction using resonance structures.
questions.a: Halogen has lone pairs that donate electron density into the ring via resonance (+R), placing negative charge at ortho/para positions. This resonance donation outweighs inductive withdrawal for orientation, making ortho/para positions more electron-rich for electrophilic attack. However, net inductive withdrawal deactivates the ring overall. A student who says "Cl is meta-directing because it withdraws electrons" has ignored resonance donation and misapplied the directing effect rule for deactivating groups (which are usually meta-directing except halogens).

questions.q: Predict the major product(s) when (a) toluene undergoes bromination with Br₂/FeBr₃, (b) nitrobenzene undergoes chlorination with Cl₂/FeCl₃. Draw structures and name them.
questions.a: (a) Toluene has -CH₃ (activating, ortho/para-directing). Major: o-bromotoluene + p-bromotoluene (para often predominates due to sterics). (b) Nitrobenzene has -NO₂ (strongly deactivating, meta-directing). Major: m-chloronitrobenzene. A wrong answer giving ortho/para for nitrobenzene or meta for toluene shows failure to apply activating/deactivating group directing effects from Class 11 hydrocarbons.

questions.q: Compare the relative rates of electrophilic bromination for benzene, chlorobenzene, and phenol. Rank them fastest to slowest and justify using substituent effects.
questions.a: Phenol > Benzene > Chlorobenzene. Phenol has -OH (strongly activating, +R >> -I), benzene has no substituent, chlorobenzene has -Cl (deactivating, -I > +R). A student ranking chlorobenzene > benzene has missed that halogen's net effect is deactivating despite ortho/para direction.

questions.q: A student attempts to prepare iodobenzene by heating benzene with I₂ and FeCl₃. The reaction fails. Explain why and write the correct reagent combination for iodination.
questions.a: Iodination is reversible: C₆H₆ + I₂ ⇌ C₆H₅I + HI. HI reduces I₂ to I⁻, shifting equilibrium left. An oxidising agent (HNO₃, HIO₄) is needed to remove HI as I₂ + H₂O. Correct: Benzene + I₂ + conc. HNO₃ (or HIO₄) at 373 K. A student who says "use FeCl₃ like chlorination" doesn't understand the thermodynamic limitation unique to iodine.

questions.q: Design a two-step synthesis of p-bromonitrobenzene starting from benzene. Write reagents for each step and explain the order.
questions.a: Step 1: Benzene + Br₂/FeBr₃ → bromobenzene (ortho/para mixture, separable). Step 2: Bromobenzene + conc. HNO₃/conc. H₂SO₄ → p-bromonitrobenzene (major) + o-bromonitrobenzene. Order matters: bromination first because -Br is ortho/para-directing; nitration first would give m-nitrobromobenzene (wrong isomer). A poor answer reversing the order or using Sandmeyer for bromination shows lack of synthetic planning.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Haloarenes (aryl halides) are prepared by ______ aromatic substitution where a hydrogen atom on the benzene ring is replaced by a halogen (Cl, Br) using halogen (Cl₂, Br₂) in the presence of a Lewis acid catalyst (FeCl₃, AlCl₃, FeBr₃) or via the Sandmeyer reaction where a diazonium salt (from primary aromatic amine + NaNO₂/HCl) reacts with CuCl/CuBr (for Cl, Br) or KI (for I).
Fill in the blank: Observe how chlorine gas passed into benzene with a pinch of anhydrous FeCl₃ in a lab fume hood yields ______ — a colourless liquid with a sweet smell used in pesticide synthesis.
What is Haloarenes (aryl halides)? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Haloarenes (aryl halides) are prepared by electrophilic aromatic substitution where a hydrogen atom on the benzene ring is replaced by a halogen (Cl, Br) using halogen (Cl₂, Br₂) in the presence of a Lewis acid catalyst (FeCl₃, AlCl₃, FeBr₃) or via the Sandmeyer reaction where a diazonium salt (from primary aromatic amine + NaNO₂/HCl).

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Haloarenes (aryl halides)?
questions.a: Students often write the Sandmeyer reaction for chlorination as "C₆H₅NH₂ + NaNO₂/HCl → C₆H₅Cl" omitting the diazonium salt intermediate and CuCl catalyst.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: Student can: (1) write balanced equations for chlorination/bromination of benzene and substituted benzenes with correct catalysts and conditions, (2) predict ortho/para product ratio and explain why halogen is ortho/para-directing despite being deactivating, (3) design a Sandmeyer reaction sequence from aniline to a specific haloarene.
